Why the Google Photos license agreement is keeping me out
It was hard with all the glowing reviews of Google's new photo feature to find something that considered privacy this morning, but I have found something and here it is!

Most free, online EULA's have something very similar to this. I think the part about:

When you upload, submit, store, send or receive content to or through our Services, you give Google (and those we work with) a worldwide license to use, host, store, reproduce, modify, create derivative works (such as those resulting from translations, adaptations or other changes we make so that your content works better with our Services), communicate, publish, publicly perform, publicly display and distribute such content.

Is just a "cya" for being able to legally move your uploaded content to servers all around the world (and to compress/modify the files). I doubt Google would use your photos in ads without your explicit consent as it would just be a PR nightmare if nothing else.

You're the explanation that makes the most sense to me. Data laws in nearly every single country are insane. There's some weird thing that was put in because someone didn't fully understand what encryption was, or what http is.
